name: The Meeker household at 1815 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_meeker_arthur

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1815 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1815 Mr. & Mrs. Arthur Meeker.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1815, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. A house of this kind kept live-in staff, and the 1900 and 1910 censuses name them; neither was read for this card, so no staff are listed. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

occupation.note: Wikipedia's article on his son calls the father an executive of Armour & Co., retired in 1928; it does not date the post, so 1904 is inferred.

persons.name: Grace Murray Meeker
persons.note: The Blue Book prints her as Mrs. Arthur Meeker; her own name is from Wikipedia's article on her son.

persons.name: Arthur Meeker jr.

born.note: Born in Chicago on 3 November 1902 (Wikipedia); the later novelist of Prairie Avenue.

persons.note: A child of twenty months on the scene date. Wikipedia says 'the family lived on Prairie Avenue' without a number; the Blue Book puts his parents at 1815, so his place here is inferred from theirs. He had three sisters, whom the article does not name or date, so they are not on this card.
